column2: req_desc

Season programme stage
The public programme page shows every published season, in date order, as a full-screen stage segment with its title, dates and a schedule rail whose rows give each screening's local time, auditorium code and seats left, and each row opens that screening.

Iris Pull scroll mapping
Within each season's 1000-pixel scroll segment, the iris openness, blade rotation, f-stop readout, schedule rail fade and ground tint follow the published formulas of scroll position exactly, in both scroll directions.

Active season and shareable URL
The active season follows the published activation rule and is reflected in the `season` query parameter, the root `data-active-season` attribute, the season tab's current state and one polite announcement, and a shared link lands on the published scroll position.

Reduced motion and renderer fallbacks
Under reduced motion the stage shows the selected season fully open with instant tab switching, and without WebGL or after a lost WebGL context an SVG iris renders the same states with the published attribute values.

In-place language switch
The language button switches every visible string, the page language and the locale path between English and French without reloading the page, remembers the choice, and moves the seat map by no more than the published tolerance.

Sale times in Montréal business time
Each season's member-priority and public-sale opening instants are 10:00 America/Toronto on their published dates and are shown in Toronto time whatever the server or browser time zone.

Guest booking journey
A guest patron picks seats on the seat map, holds them, pays with name and email only, and lands on the Booking confirmed page with tickets, a price summary and a private booking link.

Seat holds and server expiry
A seat hold lasts the configured hold time judged by the server with an exclusive end, after which payment is refused, the seats return to sale and the countdown matches the server.

Admission tax and uplift arithmetic
GST and QST are computed per admission line in integer cents with half-up rounding, the supporter uplift is an untaxed line, and the quote, booking, confirmation email, Kill Bill invoice and CSV agree to the cent.

One Kill Bill invoice per booking
Every paid booking is one Kill Bill invoice on the patron's account with the published item descriptions and one successful purchase payment equal to the amount paid now, or no payment when that amount is zero.

Checkout and gift idempotency
Checkout and gift purchase require an idempotency key, and a replay returns the original response without a second charge or email while a reused key with a different body is rejected.

Booking confirmation email
Each paid booking delivers exactly one confirmation email to Mailpit in the booking's locale with the published subject and the seat, ticket, tax, uplift, credit and total lines.

Guest booking links
A guest's booking link carries an unguessable token scoped to one booking, and it stops working when the booking is refunded or a new link is issued through the booking-link form.

Checkout succeeds whole or not at all
When Kill Bill fails during checkout no charge stands, the hold and booking stay exactly as they were, and the confirmation email is queued only together with a successful payment.

Last-seat winner and honest notices
Of simultaneous hold requests for the same seat exactly one succeeds, the others get the seat-taken result and notice, an expired hold shows the hold-expired notice, and seats left is never negative.

Member fares and priority booking
Members book at member and member-guest fares within their tier's allowance and alone may hold seats while a season is in member priority, while non-members get the published refusal.

Seat map keyboard grid
The seat map is a single tab stop moved with arrow, Home and End keys and toggled with Space or Enter, exposing each seat's code, selection and availability.

Keyboard-only member booking
A member completes the whole booking from the season tabs through the seat map, fares, uplift, step-up and payment with the keyboard alone, and the stage reaches the same end values as with a pointer.

Supporter uplift control
The uplift switch reveals preset and custom amounts with a sliding thumb, and a custom amount outside the published range is refused with the published field message in both locales.

Step-up code limits
Spending stored credit or changing tier requires an emailed six-digit code, with the published attempt ceiling, resend spacing, send limit, lockout window, Retry-After header and a response within five seconds.

Stored credit at checkout
A member's credit balance is applied to the next charge up to its total, recorded as paired ledger movements that match the Kill Bill account credit, including the zero-payment case.

Pay control states
The pay button shows the published label with the amount due in each locale, is disabled under each published condition, and shows the published pending label while a charge is in flight.

Join a membership
A signed-in patron chooses a tier and billing cadence, joins through a Kill Bill subscription on the published plan, and sees Membership active with the first invoice amount from Kill Bill.

Option menu focus
Opening the fare or billing-cadence menu moves focus to the selected option, arrow keys and Enter choose, and Escape closes the menu and returns focus to its opener.

Tier change timing
Moving to a higher tier changes the Kill Bill subscription immediately, moving to a lower tier or another cadence of the same tier takes effect at the end of the term, and the published conflicts are rejected.

Proration read from Kill Bill
The amounts shown for a tier change on screen, in the API and in the email are the Kill Bill invoice's items and amount, never a local recalculation.

Membership emails
Joining, redeeming a gift and changing tier each deliver exactly one membership email to Mailpit in the member's locale with the published subject and the tier, cadence, date and amount lines.

Gift membership purchase
A guest or signed-in patron buys a gift membership for a recipient, is charged the tier's annual price in Kill Bill, and the purchaser and recipient each receive their published email.

Single-use gift redemption
A gift's redemption link carries an unguessable token, redeems at most once even under simultaneous attempts, and answers not found once redeemed.

Gift subscription start
Redeeming a gift starts exactly one Kill Bill subscription on the tier's gift plan for the redeemer, whose first invoice amount is 0.00, while the purchaser's charge stays the tier's annual price.

Patron record ownership
A patron requesting another patron's booking, gift or hold by identifier gets exactly the same not-found response as for a record that does not exist.

Group booking journey
A signed-in organiser holds 10 to 40 seats at the group fare, names two to six payers with seat counts, pays once, and the group is checked in at the door by booking reference.

Exact group cost split
Payer shares are computed from the Kill Bill invoice total by seat count with the published largest-remainder rule and always sum exactly to the total.

Door list
The door list for a screening shows and returns only the published fields per ticket, never a patron's email, phone, full name, payment or membership details.

Single check-in and door window
Each ticket checks in at most once even from two devices at the same time, and only inside the published window around showtime.

Season lifecycle
Seasons follow the published state machine with time-driven member-priority and on-sale states, and every illegal transition is refused with the published conflict.

Weekly slots across daylight saving
Weekly screenings created from one local start time keep that Montréal wall-clock time on every occurrence across the 1 November 2026 change, following the published rule for missing and repeated times.

Season withdrawal
Withdrawing a season refunds each paid booking through Kill Bill, ends its holds, emails each holder in their locale and records each refund in the audit list.

Programmer console journey
A programmer creates a draft season, adds weekly screenings, schedules it and later archives or withdraws it from the staff console.

Finance desk journey
A finance officer finds a booking, ticket, gift or account by identifier in the staff lookup and reaches its refund and goodwill-credit controls, with the published not-found copy for misses.

Finance refunds
Finance refunds a paid booking before the refund cutoff through a Kill Bill refund, returning the paid portion to the payment and any credit portion to the member's credit, with the published amount shape.

Goodwill credits
A goodwill credit issued by finance creates a Kill Bill account credit, one paired ledger movement and one audit entry, and the account's balance equals the sum of its ledger movements.

Staff role enforcement
Finance, door and programming endpoints are refused server-side to every other role with the published forbidden response, whatever the interface shows.

Append-only audit list
Every refund, goodwill credit, reconciliation acceptance, season withdrawal and enquiry reply records actor, action, target, amount, reason and time, and no one can edit or delete an entry.

Business-day reconciliation
The reconciliation for a date covers the Toronto business day from local midnight to local midnight and compares local takings with Kill Bill payments and refunds using the published figures.

Reconciliation CSV export
The reconciliation CSV has the published columns and rows, totals that match the reconciliation, and neutralises patron-supplied names and notes that begin with formula characters.

Accepting the Kill Bill figure
When a day does not match, finance accepts Kill Bill's figure with a reason, sees the published confirmation and the day shows as accepted with an audit entry.

Accounts and sign-in return
Patrons create accounts and sign in, and after sign-in they return only to a safe same-origin path, falling back to their account page otherwise.

Self-service refunds
A patron refunds their own paid booking from the booking page or private link until the published cutoff before showtime, after which the refund is refused and only finance goodwill credit remains.

Contact enquiry and staff reply
A patron sends a contact enquiry, sees the published acknowledgement, and finance replies from the console so that exactly one reply email arrives in Mailpit in the enquiry's locale.

Service notices and recovery
When Kill Bill or the mail service is unreachable at boot or later, the app keeps serving, shows the named notice within ten seconds and clears it within ten seconds of the service returning, without a restart.

Billing outage changes nothing
While Kill Bill is unreachable, every money-moving or booking-changing request is refused with the published unavailable response and leaves bookings, holds, memberships, gifts and credits unchanged, as qualified in Services.

Mail outbox retry and drain order
Mail that cannot be sent is kept in an outbox and retried on the published ordered schedule with an attempt ceiling, then delivered oldest first exactly once per message key after recovery.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from the run manifest on the published port and answers the health check while dependencies are down.

Nothing private leaves the server
No service credential or internal host reaches the browser, and emails contain only the published identifiers and links.

Bilingual errors and emails
Every API error message and every email exists in English and French and is delivered in the published locale under the locale rule.

Responsive layouts and narrow disclosures
Every screen works at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 without horizontal scrolling, and on narrow screens the menu and film notes open through their published disclosure buttons.

Focus, hover and transition rules
Every page's first Tab stop is the skip link, dismissing a notice lands focus on the page heading, focus and hover states are visible, and interface transitions run in the published time range or instantly under reduced motion.

Projection-booth look
The public pages read as a near-black projection booth with warm off-white type, one tungsten amber for live state, serif season titles and monospaced numerals, and the iris looks like a mechanical lens diaphragm.

Real integrations in source
The source talks to Kill Bill, SMTP and Postgres for real, reads every credential from the environment, and keeps no fake state or test-only endpoint.
/app/run.json exists and is exactly one JSON object with string keys _schema (value run-manifest-v1), install, build and serve, and no other keys.

/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md has one entry per shipped package (the production tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json, including the database driver) and per bundled font, each giving name, exact version and SPDX licence identifier.
Every shipped package and font is licensed under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or OFL-1.1.
All application, build and tooling code is TypeScript; no .js, .mjs, .cjs or .jsx file exists under /app outside /app/node_modules/ and the build output /app/dist/.
No extra datastore: package.json dependencies include none of sqlite3, better-sqlite3, redis, ioredis, mongodb, mongoose, lowdb, nedb, level, and no *.db or *.sqlite file exists under /app.
No file under /app/dist/ references fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com, cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com or cdnjs.cloudflare.com.
